key_insight: The paper proposes an entangled two-electron sensor on superfluid helium that could achieve quantum-enhanced sensitivity for particle-physics detection beyond classical limits.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a scalable quantum-hardware sensing platform using microfabricated helium traps, leveraging long coherence and low impurity environments for rare-event detection.
method: Model two trapped electrons in a helium double-well geometry with both spatial and spin degrees of freedom.
Use entanglement between the electron pair to enhance measurement sensitivity.
Map the concept to particle-physics sensing use cases aligned with DRD5/CERN goals.
evidence_signal: The abstract is conceptual and theoretical, outlining formalism and motivation rather than reporting experimental data or benchmark results.
watch_item: The main implementation risk is experimentally realizing stable, controllable entangled electron pairs on helium with sufficient readout fidelity and trap scalability.
paper_title: Electrons on Helium and Entangled Quantum Sensors for Particle Physics
